question: What does epidemiological prevalence measure in a population?

options.A: Total deaths caused by a disease

explanation: Prevalence measures the total number of existing cases, both old and new, in a population at a specific time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is prevalence particularly useful for community health planning?

options.A: It measures the speed of a new infection
options.B: It calculates the genetic risk of disease transmission
options.C: It predicts the exact day an epidemic will end
options.D: It shows the total disease burden for resource planning

explanation: Knowing the total burden helps nurses and administrators allocate appropriate medical supplies and personnel. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: Point prevalence measures a health condition at what timeframe?

options.B: Over a period of ten years
options.D: A single specific point in time

explanation: Point prevalence looks at a frozen moment in time, like a snapshot of existing cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h2)

question: A study tracking malaria cases over a full six-month rainy season measures what type of prevalence?
explanation: Measuring disease status over a span of time rather than a single day represents period prevalence. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h2)

question: What forms the denominator when calculating disease prevalence?
explanation: The denominator must include all individuals in the defined group who are susceptible to having the condition. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: A village of 1,000 people has 50 existing cases of hypertension on screening day. What is the point prevalence?
explanation: Dividing 50 existing cases by 1,000 total people yields 0.05, which equals 5 percent when multiplied by 100. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: How does a very high mortality rate from a disease affect its prevalence?

options.B: It has no effect on prevalence

explanation: When patients die rapidly from a condition, they are no longer counted among the existing cases, lowering prevalence. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: Which factor will cause the prevalence of a chronic illness in a town to increase?

options.A: High death rate among diagnosed patients
options.C: Longer duration of illness before recovery or death
options.D: A sudden cure discovered for the disease

explanation: When patients live longer with a chronic disease without being cured, they remain in the pool of existing cases longer. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: What does incidence measure that prevalence does not?

options.A: The total burden of chronic illness
options.B: Only new cases of a disease

explanation: Incidence strictly counts newly developing cases, whereas prevalence counts both old and new cases together. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why is incidence better suited for investigating the immediate cause of an acute outbreak?

options.A: It captures newly developing infections directly linked to recent exposures
options.B: It counts people who have lived with the disease for decades
options.C: It measures the total financial cost of treatment
options.D: It ignores mild cases to save time

explanation: Because incidence measures new events, it helps researchers connect disease onset to recent risk factors or exposures. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h5)

question: A community health nurse uses high hypertension prevalence data to do what?

options.B: Predict the weather patterns for the upcoming farming season
options.C: Order surgical equipment for emergency appendectomies
options.D: Plan targeted blood pressure screening and education clinics

explanation: High prevalence highlights where clinical services and health education are most urgently needed. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: How can nurses use serial prevalence surveys over several years?

options.A: To diagnose individual patients during acute emergencies
options.B: To evaluate the long-term impact of community health interventions
options.C: To determine the exact genetic sequence of a pathogen
options.D: To replace standard hospital admission records

explanation: Comparing prevalence data across years shows whether disease control programmes are successfully lowering disease burden. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of using prevalence to study rapidly fatal diseases?

options.B: It is impossible to calculate a mathematical fraction
options.C: Patients die quickly and are missed in point-in-time counts
options.D: Prevalence rates will always equal one hundred percent

explanation: Fast-killing conditions result in few existing cases at any given moment, leading prevalence to underestimate the disease's true impact. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h7)

question: Why is it difficult to determine cause and effect using prevalence data?

options.A: It measures existing cases at one time without showing which came first
options.B: It relies exclusively on hospital mortality records
options.C: It only counts healthy individuals who never get sick
options.D: It requires complete genetic mapping of every participant

explanation: Because prevalence captures a snapshot of current status, it cannot easily prove whether an exposure caused the disease or followed it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h7)
